# Blackline 0.15.44

## Remote control: how far away their machine is

A session now measures its own input round trip — the time from an input leaving this device to the
far side saying it has it, on the link it actually runs on. It is shown beside the control hint, to
the person controlling, who is the one who feels it.

It is labelled as the input round trip and nothing more. It is **not** photon-to-photon: the picture
comes back over the video path, and the only honest way to measure that is a camera pointed at a
screen. A number that claimed to be the whole loop would be a guess wearing a decimal point.

The far side acknowledges before it injects, so the reading is of the link rather than of how long
that machine took to move a pointer. One batch is timed at a time, so no keystroke ever waits for an
answer, and the reading is smoothed across four samples so a single hiccup does not become the
number.

## Also

This is the first build published through the update system, so it is also the proof that it works:
0.15.43 found it, checked its signature against the key compiled into 0.15.43, checked the
installer against the hash in the signed manifest, and installed it.
